session_summary: Evaluated state transitions and edge-case behaviors on the Ember Forge route. Confirmed repeated walk commands against stationary obstacles correctly trigger telemetry events and state penalties (damage), and successfully resolve upon proper jump input.

observations.evidence: Repeated walk actions against step 2 (telemetry shows obstacle_hit with 8 damage twice) before the player successfully performed a jump action.
observations.recommendation: Ensure state validation cleanly prevents redundant movement command queuing when an obstacle state flag is active.

bugs.title: Repeated Walk Input Into Obstacle Spams Damage
repro_steps: Walk forward to step 2 where an obstacle is present
Issue 'walk' command multiple times consecutively without jumping
bugs.expected: The player should hit the obstacle once, take damage once, and be blocked from passing until jumping.
bugs.observed: The telemetry records multiple consecutive 'obstacle_hit' events (damage: 8) for duplicate walk attempts at the same step before jumping.

feature_requests.title: Explicit Input Buffering Feedback for Obstacles
feature_requests.player_value: Clearer visual or textual feedback when movement inputs are rejected due to an active blocking hazard.
feature_requests.rationale: Helps edge-case testers distinguish between input lag and intended path blocking.
feature_requests.desired_outcome: Add explicit descriptive hints when invalid movement commands collide with static hazards.

keep: Clean telemetry event logging for obstacle hits and jumps
Reliable route completion states and coin reward payouts
focus: state transitions, repeatability, blocking states, exploit risks and regressions
